Build a Synoptic Table of Diagnostic, Constant and Dominant Species

Source: R/synoptic_table.R
synoptic_table.Rd

Constructs a synoptic table for groups of vegetation releves, combining species fidelity from a previously calculated indicspecies::multipatt() result with species constancy and dominance derived from an original species-cover matrix.

Usage

synoptic_table(
  veg,
  groups,
  phi,
  alpha = 0.05,
  phi_min = 0.25,
  constancy_min = 40,
  dominant_freq_min = 50,
  dominant_cover_min = 25,
  include = c("diagnostic", "constant", "dominant"),
  dominance_rule = c("high_cover_frequency", "presence_frequency_and_max_cover")
)

Arguments

veg

Numeric matrix or data frame of vegetation records, with releves in rows and species in columns. Values are original cover estimates; zero indicates absence. Species names must be supplied as column names.

groups

Vector of group membership, one element per releve in veg. May be numeric, character, or a factor. Named vectors are aligned to the row names of veg when possible.

phi

Complete object returned by indicspecies::multipatt(), calculated externally with func = "r.g", duleg = TRUE, and presence/absence vegetation data. Must contain phi$sign.

alpha

Maximum p-value for diagnostic species (default 0.05).

phi_min

Minimum fidelity statistic for diagnostic species (default 0.25).

constancy_min

Minimum species frequency within a group, in percent, for classification as constant (default 40).

dominant_freq_min

Minimum percentage of releves meeting the selected dominance rule (default 50).

dominant_cover_min

Cover threshold for high cover, expressed in the same units as veg (default 25).

include

Character vector selecting the retained species categories: any of "diagnostic", "constant", and "dominant". By default, all three categories are included.

dominance_rule

Character string specifying how dominant species are defined. "high_cover_frequency" (default) requires high cover in a minimum proportion of releves; "presence_frequency_and_max_cover" requires sufficient occurrence frequency and high cover at least once.

Value

A list with the following components:

synoptic

Main synoptic data frame, with one row per retained species-group combination. Columns are group, species, diagnostic, phi, p.value, frequency, constant, high_cover_frequency, max_cover, dominant, and a percentage-frequency column for each group (such as G1, G2).

diagnostic

Data frame containing the diagnostic associations retained by the fidelity and significance thresholds.

frequency

Species-by-group numeric matrix of percentage occurrence frequencies.

constant

Species-by-group logical matrix of constancy.

dominant

Species-by-group logical matrix of dominance.

high_cover_frequency

Species-by-group numeric matrix of the percentage of releves at or above dominant_cover_min.

max_cover

Species-by-group numeric matrix of maximum cover.

phi

Unmodified multipatt() object supplied to the function.

presence_absence

Presence/absence data frame derived from veg.

settings

List of thresholds and options used to generate the synoptic table. Does not include the external permutation settings.

Details

The input veg must have releves in rows and species in columns. The groups vector assigns each releve to a vegetation group. If groups is a named vector, its elements are reordered to match rownames(veg).

Diagnostic species: Species are flagged as diagnostic if the supplied multipatt() output meets both stat >= phi_min and p.value <= alpha. The phi argument must contain the complete result from indicspecies::multipatt() previously computed on the presence/absence transformation of veg, using func = "r.g" and duleg = TRUE. The species order in phi$sign must match colnames(veg), and the group-index order must match the order used by this function. The function does not calculate Phi, permute data, or call multipatt() itself.

Constant species: The percentage frequency of each species in each group is calculated from veg > 0. Species with frequency at least constancy_min are classified as constant.

Dominant species: Dominance is assessed using the original species cover values. With dominance_rule = "high_cover_frequency", a species is dominant if it reaches dominant_cover_min cover in at least dominant_freq_min percent of the group's releves. With dominance_rule = "presence_frequency_and_max_cover", the species must occur in at least dominant_freq_min percent of the group's releves and reach dominant_cover_min in at least one releve.

The include argument selects which categories of species are retained. Selection is inclusive (logical OR): satisfying any requested category is sufficient. A species may be diagnostic, constant, and dominant at the same time. All output rows are sorted by group and then by diagnostic status, dominance, constancy, frequency, Phi, and species name.

The function does not accept permutation settings such as nperm or seed: set these when computing phi externally. A different choice of reporting thresholds can reuse the same phi object, as long as the underlying species data and groups remain unchanged.

References

Guarino, R., Caldarella, O., Gristina, A. S., Marcenò, C., & Gianguzzi, L. (2026). Broom-dominated shrublands of Sicily: revisiting the syntaxonomy of the Cytisetea scopario-striati at the south-eastern margin of their range. Vegetation Classification and Survey, 7, 127-148. doi:10.3897/VCS.183815 .

See also

multipatt

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Small illustrative dataset: releves in rows, species in columns
veg <- data.frame(
  Festuca = c(60, 45, 51, 50, 0, 2, 0, 3),
  Bromus = c(0, 0, 1, 2, 35, 43, 38, 29),
  Poa = c(2, 3, 0, 4, 5, 3, 0, 2)
)
rownames(veg) <- paste0("R", seq_len(nrow(veg)))
groups <- rep(1:2, each = 4)

# Calculate fidelity externally, using presence/absence data
set.seed(123)
phi <- indicspecies::multipatt(
  (veg > 0) * 1,
  groups,
  func = "r.g",
  duleg = TRUE,
  control = permute::how(nperm = 99)
)

# Build the synoptic table using original cover values
res <- synoptic_table(veg, groups, phi)
res$synoptic
res$diagnostic
res$frequency

# Apply a more restrictive filter without recalculating phi
res2 <- synoptic_table(
  veg, groups, phi,
  phi_min = 0.4,
  constancy_min = 60,
  include = c("diagnostic", "constant")
)
res2$synoptic
} # }
